name: Battle Bowl: May Day '98

appearances.source: The fed's own Battle Bowl battle royal broadcast, a ten-plus entrant over-the-top-rope elimination match recounted in prose rather than a two-sided match.

matches.note: USCW Television Title, Weapons and Cage match -- the fed's own first. Abyss won after his own manager sabotaged the cage's bolts, dropping a steel panel on Shining Path.
USCW Light Heavyweight Title, three-way. Daniel Stephens ran in and struck Kid Sharpe from behind, letting Shawn Evans pin him for the title.
USCW Tag Team Title. Mopreme never entered the match; Seagram wrestled alone and pinned Dana Czech after a rival wrestler's interference with a bat.
Non-title cage match. Viper and Sinister won after setting a table on fire and driving Syncho through it; both hWo members required medical attention.
USCW Heavyweight Title, tournament final. Sinister ran in, knocked out the referee's replacement count-keeper Ron Matthews, and rolled Viper on top for the pin.

notes: The Battle Bowl battle royal (won by Chris Evans of the Marauders for $50,000 and a future Heavyweight Title shot) is recounted in the page's own prose as a many-entrant over-the-top-rope elimination match rather than structured as a two-sided match. After the show, the fed's own president had Daniel Dare ambush new Heavyweight Champion Viper in the president's own hotel suite, citing a year-old rivalry between Dare and Viper from another promotion.

name: Midweek Madness

matches.note: USCW Television Title. Mike Adams submitted Tony Dylan to become the new champion.
USCW North American Title. David Dobouis ended Scott Dakota's undefeated streak and title reign with a finisher called the Bad Mojo.

notes: This card also carried three further undercard results (The Bishop over Elwood J. Blues by DQ; Jason Polo over Juice; Joe Mills over Shining Path) not structured -- none of the three wrestlers not already minted from Battle Bowl are minted here, consistent with the accession's own budget.
